description: Website Copywriter — AI-Assisted, Direct Response, SEO & Conversion Focused Remote | Full-Time or Part-Time Work Hours: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM AWST --- PLEASE READ BEFORE APPLYING This is not a role for blog writers, academic writers, or anyone who thinks website copy is about filling pages with words. We are looking for a Website Copywriter who understands: - How to write website copy that makes people take action — not just read - Direct response principles — headlines, hooks, CTAs, objection handling, urgency - SEO copywriting that sounds like a human wrote it — meta titles, meta descriptions, heading hierarchy, keyword integration, search intent, local SEO, internal linking, image alt text - How Google actually ranks content now — natural language, topical depth, and relevance. Not keyword stuffing. If you still think SEO means cramming the same phrase into every paragraph, stop here. - How to use AI writing tools (Claude, ChatGPT) to draft faster, then rewrite and humanise the output until it sounds like a real person who knows what they are talking about - How to work inside Figma — placing and editing copy within actual page designs, not just handing over a Google Doc If you can write website copy for service-based businesses that ranks, converts, and sounds like it was written by someone who actually understands the business — keep reading. --- WHAT YOU'LL DO You will write website copy for service-based businesses across trades, health, real estate, professional services, events, and more. Every page you write has two jobs: rank in search and convert the person who lands on it. You will work within our AI-assisted workflow. You will use Claude, ChatGPT, and our internal prompts to generate drafts and frameworks, then rewrite, sharpen, and humanise the output. The final copy must read like a sharp human wrote it — not a machine. You will work directly inside Figma. You place your copy into the actual website designs so the build team works from one source of truth instead of cross-referencing separate documents. Here is what the day-to-day looks like: - Write homepage, service page, about page, landing page, and location page copy for client websites - Write above-the-fold value propositions — the headline, subheadline, and CTA a visitor sees before they scroll - Write benefit-driven body copy that speaks to what the customer wants, not just what the business does - Write objection-handling copy — anticipating why someone might hesitate and addressing it before they leave - Write risk-reversal copy — guarantees, free quotes, no-obligation language that lowers friction - Write social proof sections — testimonial intros, case study summaries, credibility stacks (certifications, awards, years in business) - Write CTAs that actually say something — not just "Contact Us" but specific, benefit-driven actions that match the page - Write micro-copy — form labels, placeholder text, button text, thank you pages, confirmation messages - Write FAQ sections that handle objections, build trust, and support schema markup - Write SEO-optimised meta titles and meta descriptions for every page — click-worthy, within character limits, and aligned with search intent - Write heading hierarchy properly — one H1 per page, logical H2 and H3 structure that reflects what the searcher is looking for and what Google needs to understand the page - Write keyword-mapped copy that integrates primary and secondary keywords naturally — like a normal person talking about the topic, not like someone trying to game an algorithm - Write image alt text that is descriptive and accessible, not stuffed with keywords - Write internal linking anchor text — connecting service pages, location pages, and supporting content with natural, relevant anchors - Write URL slug recommendations — short, clean, keyword-relevant - Write location and service area pages for local SEO — suburb-specific, city-specific pages that are genuinely useful and unique. Not the same page with the suburb name swapped out. - Write to search intent — you know whether a page needs to answer a question, compare options, or drive an action, and you structure the copy accordingly - Write content that can target featured snippets — structured lists, direct answers, table-format content where it fits - Structure FAQ and review content to support schema markup - Use AI tools to draft faster — then rewrite everything until it reads naturally and sounds specific to the business - Work inside Figma to place copy directly into designs, not in a separate doc - Adapt tone and voice across industries — a plumber's website does not sound like a cosmetic clinic - Turn around copy quickly and accurately — this is a fast-paced agency, not a leisurely content mill --- OUR APPROACH TO SEO COPY This is important, so read it carefully. We do not keyword stuff. Ever. Google uses natural language processing to understand content. It reads context, synonyms, related terms, and topical depth. It does not count how many times you jammed a keyword into a paragraph. We expect you to understand this. We expect you to write copy that covers a topic thoroughly and naturally — the way a genuine expert in that field would explain it to a potential customer. That is what ranks. That is what converts. That is what we do. If you still write SEO copy by repeating exact-match phrases in every heading and every second sentence, this role is not for you. What we expect: - You understand that Google rewards topical authority, not keyword repetition - You write naturally and let keywords sit where they belong — in headings, in the first paragraph, in anchor text — without forcing them - You cover related subtopics, synonyms, and questions a real searcher would have - You structure content so Google can understand it (heading hierarchy, FAQ structure, clear topic flow) without making it read like it was written for a crawler - You know the difference between writing for the person searching and writing for the search engine — and you know the best SEO copy does both at the same time --- MUST-HAVE EXPERIENCE (NON-NEGOTIABLE) - Proven experience writing website copy for service-based businesses — homepage, service pages, landing pages, about pages, location pages. Not blogs. Not social captions. Not product descriptions. - Direct response copywriting skills — you can write a headline that stops someone, a subheadline that pulls them deeper, body copy that handles objections, and a CTA that gets them to act. - SEO copywriting that sounds human — you can integrate keywords naturally, write proper meta titles and descriptions, structure headings correctly, write internal linking anchors, and build location pages that are genuinely unique. You understand search intent and you write to it. - A modern understanding of how Google ranks content — you know that natural language, topical depth, and content quality matter more than keyword density. You do not stuff keywords. Full stop. - Experience using AI writing tools — you have used Claude, ChatGPT, or similar. You can prompt well, get useful output, and then rewrite it until it sounds like a human who knows the subject. - Figma proficiency — you can navigate Figma, find the right frames, and place or edit copy directly in website designs. You do not need to be a designer but you need to be comfortable in the tool. - Excellent written English — native or near-native level. Grammar, spelling, punctuation, and sentence structure must be flawless. - Ability to adapt tone and voice — you can write for a tradesperson and a luxury brand on the same day without the copy sounding identical. - Self-editing discipline — you proofread your own work before submitting. You do not rely on someone else to catch mistakes. If your experience is only blogs, social media, or academic writing — this is not the right fit. If you copy-paste AI output without rewriting it — this is not the right fit. If your idea of SEO is repeating a keyword as many times as possible — this is not the right fit. --- NICE TO HAVE - Experience writing for Australian businesses or audiences - Familiarity with GoHighLevel landing pages - Understanding of CRO principles — heatmaps, A/B testing insights, scroll depth - Experience with keyword research tools (Ahrefs, SEMrush, Ubersuggest) or working from keyword briefs - Familiarity with NLP-related SEO concepts — entity salience, TF-IDF, topical relevance scoring -
